messages:
Jordan (CS): Customer reports intermittent 403 / 'Billing required' in the UI when saving a project. Happens in Chrome and Brave, not consistent. They can sometimes reproduce by clicking Save twice fast. Need minimal repro bundle (network + console + headers + curl).
Eli (Eng): thanks. ask them for the full HAR + a net-export (netlog) if possible — helps with TLS/socket timing and edge proxies. also request the response headers (x-request-id).
Jordan (CS): they've given one screenshot and a timestamp (2026-03-16T18:04:12Z). i'll ask them for steps and the files. want a short instruction set i can paste?
Priya (Support): paste this to customer, short and numbered. include redaction note.
Priya (Support): 1) Reproduce the issue in Chrome or Edge and keep DevTools open. 2) In DevTools > Network: check "Preserve log" and "Disable cache". Right-click any request -> Save all as HAR with content. 3) Capture console logs: DevTools > Console -> right-click -> "Save as..." (or select all, copy, paste into a text file). 4) Capture netlog (optional but super helpful): open chrome://net-export/ -> Start Logging to Disk -> reproduce -> Stop -> attach the .json. 5) From the failing request response headers, copy the value of "x-request-id" (or any "request-id" header) and paste it in your reply. 6) Run this curl (replace your key, redact it before sharing):
```bash
export TOKEN=REDACTED
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/save 
  -d '{"name":"test","payload":"..."}'
```
This prints response headers and body; include the headers block (the first lines starting with HTTP/). 7) Tell us: browser + version, OS, exact local time when you reproduced, and whether any company VPN/proxy was active. 8) Zip up HAR + netlog + console.txt and upload to the support upload link or reply here.
Eli (Eng): add: if possible, enable verbose logging in the browser profile: DevTools > Network > right-click header area -> "Copy -> Copy as cURL" and include that cURL too. net-export helps diagnose connection resets, TLS handshakes, and proxy 502/403 conversions.
Jordan (CS): customer sent a HAR but no netlog or request-id. they said "I tried saving twice fast and then it failed". i'll ask them to run the curl and provide headers.
Priya (Support): mention redaction rules to customer: replace the token with "<REDACTED_TOKEN>" and remove any user PII in payloads. we only need request ids, timestamps, and the raw headers.
Jordan (CS): customer attached har: 2MB. asked for netlog steps, sent Priya's numbered list.
Support Bot: Reminder: upload quota for attachments is 150MB. If >150MB, please use the secure upload link (support.redwood/upload) and paste the share URL here.
Eli (Eng): once they upload, we will grep the HAR for status 403/401/429 and match the request-id timestamps in netlog. if we see the pattern (fast double save -> 429 or auth token expiry) we'll check the token refresh flow.
Jordan (CS): customer replied with net-export file and curl output. netlog shows a TCP FIN around the time of failure. attaching now.
Priya (Support): thanks — i'll forward to eng with the exact files and the request-id header pinned. we'll follow up with customer within 24h. :thumbsup:
Eli (Eng): received. next steps: i'll run the HAR through our local analyzer and then correlate x-request-id to our server logs. if i need a deeper capture (pcap) i'll request permission from customer.
Jordan (CS): appreciated. copying this thread into the ticket.
Priya (Support): other quick tip for customers on mac: if Console > Save as doesn't exist, press CMD+A, CMD+C and paste into a .txt, or open the Console panel (View > Developer > JavaScript Console) and copy.
Jordan (CS): closing loop — customer confirmed they replaced token with <REDACTED_TOKEN> and uploaded to the portal. we'll mark this as triaged.
